questions.question: Your team needs a single managed Azure workspace that lets data scientists train and deploy models with notebooks and the Python SDK, while business analysts use a no-code drag-and-drop designer. Which service fits best?
options: Azure AI Search (vector and keyword retrieval)
Azure Machine Learning (SDK notebooks plus Designer)
questions.explanation: Azure Machine Learning is the end-to-end managed ML platform on Azure — it provides Automated ML, the visual Designer, hosted notebooks, the Python and CLI v2 SDKs, MLOps pipelines, managed endpoints and a model registry, covering both the SDK-driven data-science persona and the no-code analyst persona in one workspace. Azure Databricks is a Spark analytics platform with collaborative notebooks but no built-in drag-and-drop model designer for non-coders. Azure Synapse Analytics is a unified analytics and data-warehouse service whose notebooks target Spark/SQL exploration rather than model training with a designer surface. Azure AI Search powers keyword and vector retrieval for search and RAG rather than model training or deployment.

questions.question: A developer wants to add vision, language, speech and decision features to an app by calling pre-built REST endpoints without training any model. Which family of Azure services should they use?
options: Azure HDInsight (managed Hadoop and Spark clusters)
questions.explanation: Azure AI services (the rebrand of Azure Cognitive Services) is the family of pre-built, consumable AI APIs grouped into Vision, Language, Speech and Decision categories — exactly the surface a developer calls without training a model. Azure Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation between stores rather than exposing AI endpoints. Azure Logic Apps builds no-code workflow integrations between SaaS connectors but does not host inference APIs of its own. Azure HDInsight provides managed Hadoop, Spark and Kafka clusters — an analytics compute plane, not a REST-callable AI product family.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning is used to predict a continuous numeric value, such as the future selling price of a house from its features?
questions.explanation: Regression is a supervised learning technique that predicts a continuous numeric value (price, temperature, demand) by learning a function from labelled examples. Classification is also supervised but returns a discrete class label — it would only bucket the house into a price band, not produce a precise value. Unsupervised clustering groups unlabelled data by similarity and never produces a numeric target prediction. Reinforcement learning learns a policy by trial and error against environment rewards, which does not fit a static "features → target price" supervised setup.

questions.question: An online retailer wants to automatically segment shoppers by purchase behaviour when no category labels are available. Which machine-learning approach is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Clustering is the unsupervised technique that groups items by feature similarity when no labels are provided — k-means partitions into a fixed k of centroids, DBSCAN discovers density-based clusters and marks noise. Supervised classification cannot run at all without labelled training data, so it is unusable on an unlabelled shopper population. Regression is also supervised and predicts a continuous number rather than assigning group membership. Anomaly detection isolates rare outlier records against a normal baseline rather than partitioning the entire population into interpretable segments.

questions.question: While preparing internal training on AI ethics, you must cite Microsoft's Responsible AI principles using Microsoft's exact published terminology. Which list uses the exact wording Microsoft publishes for its six Responsible AI principles?
options: Fairness; reliability and safety; confidentiality; inclusiveness; transparency; auditability
Fairness; reliability and safety; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability
Fairness; explainability; privacy and security; sustainability; transparency; human oversight
Reliability and safety; scalability; data minimisation; inclusiveness; interpretability; governance
questions.explanation: Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles are Fairness; Reliability and Safety; Privacy and Security; Inclusiveness; Transparency; and Accountability. The other three lists substitute vocabulary Microsoft does not use — "explainability" or "interpretability" instead of Transparency, "human oversight", "governance" or "auditability" instead of Accountability, and "confidentiality" instead of Privacy and Security. The extra terms (sustainability, scalability, data minimisation) come from adjacent frameworks such as ISO/IEC 23894 or the EU AI Act, not from Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard.

questions.question: Your application needs to detect human faces in images and analyse attributes such as head pose, with some features requiring an approved Limited Access application. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Face is the purpose-built biometric service for face detection, identification, verification and attribute analysis (including head pose); its sensitive attributes (emotion, age, gender) and identity match sit behind the Limited Access programme and require an approved application. Azure AI Vision covers general computer vision (tags, captions, OCR, dense captions) but does not offer identity matching or the Limited Access face attribute set. Azure AI Document Intelligence targets structured extraction from forms and layouts rather than human faces. Azure AI Speech operates on audio signals — no image input at all.

questions.question: Your finance team needs to pull structured fields, tables and key-value pairs out of invoices and receipts using both pre-built and custom-trained models. Which Azure service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structured fields from documents. It ships pre-built models for invoices, receipts, IDs, business cards and layout, plus custom models you train on your own document templates. Azure AI Content Safety filters harmful text and images against configurable severity thresholds — it does not parse document layout. Azure AI Translator only converts text between languages and would not extract totals or line items. Azure AI Personalizer is a decision service that ranks content variants using contextual bandits and never touches document structure.

questions.question: Which feature inside Azure AI Language scores the overall opinion in a passage of text as positive, neutral or negative with a confidence value?
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis is the Azure AI Language feature that classifies a passage as positive, neutral or negative and returns a confidence score per label, with per-aspect opinion mining available as an add-on. Key phrase extraction surfaces the main concepts in the text but is silent about whether the writer is happy or angry. Named entity recognition tags people, places, dates and other entity types rather than judging tone. Language detection only identifies which language the text is written in and returns an ISO code — not a polarity score.

questions.question: A call-centre app must transcribe live customer audio into text in real time. Which Azure AI Speech capability provides this?
questions.explanation: Speech to text converts spoken audio into written text using continuous recognition, streamed in real time or fed from recorded files, and exposes both fast and diarised variants for call-centre transcription. Text to speech is the inverse — synthesising audio from a written script — so it produces sound, not text. Speech translation converts spoken input across languages, delivering translated text or audio rather than a same-language transcript. Speaker recognition identifies or verifies a person by their voice and returns an identity match instead of a transcript.

questions.question: Your team wants to build a chatbot that answers user questions from an existing collection of FAQs, product documents and support URLs. Which Azure capability is designed for that?
options: Azure AI Metrics Advisor (business KPI monitoring)
Azure AI Anomaly Detector (time-series outlier flagging)
Azure AI Bot Service (conversational hosting framework)
Azure AI Language question answering (KB index)
questions.explanation: Question answering, a feature of Azure AI Language (the successor to QnA Maker), ingests FAQ pages, PDFs and URLs, builds an indexed knowledge base and serves natural-language answers with confidence scores. Azure AI Bot Service is the conversational hosting layer that a bot uses to expose channels (Teams, web chat, WhatsApp) — it typically calls question answering to answer FAQs but does not build the knowledge base itself. Metrics Advisor monitors KPI time series against seasonality and forecasts, not document Q&A. Anomaly Detector flags outliers in numeric time-series streams — neither service indexes documents for retrieval.

questions.question: A factory wants to flag unusual spikes in equipment-sensor time-series streams without training a model. Which Azure AI service should they use?
options: Azure AI Content Safety (text and image moderation)
Azure AI Anomaly Detector (decision API for outliers)
Azure AI Custom Vision (browser image classifier trainer)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Anomaly Detector is a pre-built decision service that finds anomalies in univariate or multivariate time-series streams with no ML expertise required — you POST the series and it returns anomaly points, expected values and severity. Azure AI Custom Vision trains custom image classifiers or object detectors and has no notion of time series. Azure AI Translator converts text between languages, and Azure AI Content Safety moderates harmful text and images — none of the other three analyse sensor waveforms for unusual patterns.

questions.question: You want to train an image classifier from a small set of labelled photos using a web portal that requires no code. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
options: Azure AI Face (face detection and analysis)
Azure AI Vision (prebuilt Image Analysis API)
Azure AI Video Indexer (multimedia content insights)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision (customvision.ai) lets you upload images, tag them, train a custom image-classification or object-detection model in the browser, and then export the model or call it via REST — all without code. Azure AI Vision only returns prebuilt tags, captions and OCR and cannot be trained on your own class labels. Azure AI Video Indexer extracts insights from video streams (transcript, faces, brands) rather than training a still-image classifier. Azure AI Face is dedicated to detecting and analysing human faces — wrong subject, and it has no training portal for arbitrary classes.

questions.question: Which Azure Machine Learning feature iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters to surface a high-quality model with minimal coding?
questions.explanation: Automated ML (AutoML) iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters and produces a leaderboard of models for classification, regression, forecasting, NLP and computer-vision tasks — the closest thing to "hands-off training" in Azure ML. Hyperdrive only tunes hyperparameters for a single training script and does not choose the algorithm. MLflow tracking simply logs runs, metrics and artefacts and never picks a model on its own. Azure ML Designer is a drag-and-drop pipeline builder where the user still selects each algorithm module manually.

questions.question: When a team ships interpretability tooling that explains why a model produced a given prediction, which Microsoft Responsible AI principle is MOST directly supported?
questions.explanation: Transparency means people can understand how the AI system works and the basis of its decisions; feature-attribution methods such as SHAP, LIME and the Responsible AI dashboard in Azure ML directly support this principle. Fairness targets biased outcomes across demographic groups rather than the mechanics behind a single prediction. Reliability and safety covers consistent, safe operation across time and inputs. Inclusiveness ensures the system serves diverse users — none of those three is specifically about explaining individual predictions.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to use OpenAI GPT models inside Azure with regional hosting, private networking, content filters and Microsoft enterprise agreements. Which service should they choose?
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI Service exposes OpenAI's GPT, embeddings, DALL·E and Whisper models hosted on Azure with enterprise-grade security, regional deployments, integrated content filters, VNet/Private Link integration and Microsoft billing. Azure AI Language ships prebuilt NLP features (sentiment, NER, translation, question answering) but does not host GPT-family models. Azure AI Search is a retrieval and indexing service that commonly pairs with Azure OpenAI in RAG patterns yet does not host the LLM itself. Azure Bot Service is a conversational hosting framework that consumes an LLM rather than being one.

questions.question: Which pattern grounds a generative AI model in current private knowledge by fetching relevant passages at inference time and passing them into the prompt, instead of changing the model weights?
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves the most relevant passages (typically via vector search over an index such as Azure AI Search) and injects them into the prompt, so the model answers using current, private content without altering its weights or requiring a training run. Fine-tuning modifies the weights themselves and needs a retraining cycle every time the knowledge changes. RLHF aligns model behaviour with human preference data at training time — it shapes style and refusals rather than injecting fresh facts at inference. Prompt compression simply squeezes an existing prompt to fewer tokens; it does not add any external knowledge.

questions.question: Which Azure AI service offers content filters that flag hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content in text and images, and is integrated with Azure OpenAI?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Content Safety analyses text and images for four harmful categories (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual) with severity levels and adds Prompt Shield and protected-material detection for generative-AI scenarios; it is the moderation layer wired into Azure OpenAI. Microsoft Purview classifies and governs data lineage across the enterprise but does not perform runtime moderation of model output. Azure AI Personalizer ranks content variants for users using contextual bandits — no harm scoring at all. Azure AI Translator only converts text between languages.

questions.question: Which Azure service is the natural choice to implement knowledge mining: indexing a large set of documents and enriching them with AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities) so users can search them?
options: Azure Data Lake Storage (raw file storage)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search) is the knowledge-mining service — it pulls documents from data sources, runs an AI-enrichment skillset (OCR, key phrases, entities, vector embeddings) and exposes a queryable Lucene-based index with keyword, hybrid and vector search. It is also the typical retriever in Azure OpenAI RAG solutions. Azure Data Lake Storage holds raw files in a hierarchical namespace but performs no indexing or enrichment. Azure Cosmos DB is an operational NoSQL database that supports point and range queries, not full-text corpus mining. Azure AI Document Intelligence extracts structured fields from an individual form but does not build a corpus-wide index.

questions.question: A model scores very high on its training data but performs poorly on new, unseen samples. What is this behaviour called?
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorised the training data (including its noise) and fails to generalise to unseen examples — the classic "good on train, bad on test" split. Mitigations include collecting more training data, regularisation, simpler models, cross-validation and early stopping. Underfitting is the opposite: the model is too simple and scores poorly on both training and test sets. Class imbalance is a skewed label distribution that biases predictions toward the majority class, but it does not by itself cause a train/test gap. Data drift is a shift in the input distribution after deployment — a post-deployment monitoring problem, not a train-vs-test-set behaviour.

questions.question: On a strongly imbalanced binary-classification problem such as credit-card fraud detection, which metric gives the most informative view of model quality?
questions.explanation: F1-score, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, is the standard classification metric on strongly imbalanced problems because it penalises both missed positives and false alarms; precision–recall curves and AUC-PR are common companions. Plain classification accuracy is misleading — predicting "not fraud" for every row still yields >99% accuracy on typical fraud data while catching zero fraud. MAE measures absolute error against a continuous target and applies to regression, not to a discrete positive/negative label. R-squared measures the fraction of variance explained by a regression model — also a regression metric, not a classification one.
